Definition: properly, to bend, i.e. (by implication) to clasp; also (reflexively) to turn around or aside
BiblicalUsage: To turn aside or to take hold is the word's work in two very different scenes. In Job 6:18 the paths of the desert caravans "are turned aside; they go to nothing, and perish," and in Judges 16:29 Samson "took hold of the two middle pillars" of the house and brought it down.
TheologicalSignificance: To my mind, the word's two senses are the two ways a life goes: paths that turn aside and come to nothing, and hands that take hold and bring the house down.
